translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 2 chi 2 cun 2 fen 77

sentences.zh: 丈一尺二寸一分八十二

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 1 chi 2 cun 1 fen 82

sentences.zh: 二十五刻四百七十五分
二十五刻四百七十五分
丈一尺二寸一分八十二

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 1 chi 2 cun 1 fen 82

sentences.zh: 丈二尺二寸二分七十七

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 2 chi 2 cun 2 fen 77

sentences.zh: 各置其氣消息衰，依定氣所有日，每以陟降率陟減、降加其分，滿百從衰，各得每日消息定衰。

translations.literal: For each, set its qi message wane; according to the days belonging to that fixed qi, for each day apply the ascension-descent rate—subtract on ascension, add on descent—the parts; when full, carry to the wane; each obtains the daily fixed message wane.
translations.idiomatic: For each seasonal node, set its message-wane constant; for each day in that fixed qi, apply the ascension-descent rate—subtract on ascension, add on descent—to the parts; carry hundreds into the wane tally to obtain the daily fixed message wane.

sentences.zh: 其距二分前後各一氣之外，陟降不等，皆以三日為限。

translations.literal: Beyond one qi on either side of the two equinoxes, where ascension and descent are unequal, all take a three-day limit.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the single qi bracketing each equinox, where ascension and descent are unequal, a three-day band limit applies throughout.

translations.literal: On the first day of Rain Water, descent 78.
On the first day of Pure Brightness, ascension 1.
On the first day of End of Heat, descent 99.
translations.idiomatic: End of Heat, day 1: descent rate 99.

translations.literal: On the first day of Cold Dew, ascension 1.

sentences.zh: 各置初日陟降率，依限次損益之，為每日率。

translations.literal: For each, set the first day’s ascension-descent rate; according to the limit bands, increase or decrease in sequence to obtain the daily rate.
translations.idiomatic: Set each first-day ascension-descent rate; step through the limit bands by increase or decrease to obtain the daily rate.

sentences.zh: 乃遞以陟減、降加氣初消息衰，各得每日定衰。

translations.literal: Then in succession subtract ascension and add descent to the qi’s initial message wane, each obtaining the daily fixed wane.
translations.idiomatic: Then successively subtract ascension and add descent from the qi’s opening message wane to obtain the daily fixed wane.

sentences.zh: 南方戴日之下，正中無晷。

translations.literal: Beneath the sub-solar point in the south, at true center there is no gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Directly beneath the sub-solar point in the south, at true noon there is no shadow.

sentences.zh: 自戴日之北一度，乃初數千三百七十九。

translations.literal: One degree north of the sub-solar point, the initial count is 1,379.
translations.idiomatic: One degree north of the sub-solar point, the initial count is 1,379.

sentences.zh: 自此起差，每度增一，終於二十五度，計增二十六分。

translations.literal: From this the difference begins; for each degree add 1, ending at 25 degrees, totaling an increase of 26 parts.
translations.idiomatic: From here the increment begins: add 1 per degree up to 25°, for a total increase of 26 parts.

sentences.zh: 又每度增二，終於四十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 2, ending at 40 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 2 per degree up to 40°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增六，終於四十四度，增六十八。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 6, ending at 44 degrees, increase 68.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 6 per degree up to 44°, increase 68.

sentences.zh: 又每度增二，終於五十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 2, ending at 50 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 2 per degree up to 50°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增七，終於五十五度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 7, ending at 55 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 7 per degree up to 55°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增十九，終於六十度，增百六十。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 19, ending at 60 degrees, increase 160.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 19 per degree up to 60°, increase 160.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十三，終於六十五度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 33, ending at 65 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 33 per degree up to 65°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十六，終於七十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 36, ending at 70 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 36 per degree up to 70°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十九，終於七十二度，增二百六十。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 39, ending at 72 degrees, increase 260.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 39 per degree up to 72°, increase 260.
Each value is the per-degree difference.

sentences.zh: 因累其差，以遞加初數，滿百為分，分十為寸，各為每度晷差。

translations.literal: Accumulate the differences in succession, adding in turn to the initial count; when full, 100 become parts, and 10 parts become cun—each is the per-degree gnomon difference.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the differences cumulatively onto the initial count; carry hundreds into parts and tens of parts into cun to obtain the per-degree gnomon difference.

sentences.zh: 又累其晷差，得戴日之北每度晷數。

translations.literal: Again accumulate the gnomon differences to obtain the gnomon count for each degree north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Sum those differences again to obtain the gnomon reading for each degree north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各置其氣去極度，以極去戴日度五十六及分八十二半減之，得戴日之北度數。

translations.literal: For each, set its qi’s departure from the pole; subtract the pole’s distance from the sub-solar point, 56 degrees and 82½ parts, to obtain the degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Set the qi’s polar distance and subtract 56° 82½ parts (the pole’s offset from the sub-solar point) to obtain degrees north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各以其消息定衰所直度之晷差，滿百為分，分十為寸，得每日晷差。

translations.literal: For each, take the gnomon difference for the degree at which the fixed message wane falls; when full, 100 become parts, and 10 parts become cun, obtaining the daily gnomon difference.
translations.idiomatic: Take the per-degree gnomon difference at the degree of the fixed message wane; carry hundreds into parts and tens into cun for the daily gnomon difference.

sentences.zh: 乃遞以息減、消加其氣初晷數，得每日中晷常數。

translations.literal: Then in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial gnomon count, obtaining the daily mean noon gnomon constant.
translations.idiomatic: Then successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening gnomon count to obtain the daily mean noon gnomon constant.

sentences.zh: 以其日所在氣定小餘，爻統減之，餘為中後分。

translations.literal: Take that day’s fixed minor remainder within its qi; subtract the line divisor; the remainder is the after-noon fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Take the day’s fixed minor remainder within its qi, subtract the line divisor, and the remainder is the after-noon fraction.

sentences.zh: 不足減，反相減，為中前分。

translations.literal: If insufficient to subtract, reverse and subtract to obtain the before-noon fraction.
translations.idiomatic: If it will not subtract, reverse the subtraction to obtain the before-noon fraction.

sentences.zh: 以其晷差乘之，如通法而一，為變差。

translations.literal: Multiply by its gnomon difference; as one per universal divisor, obtaining the variation difference.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the gnomon difference, divide by the universal divisor, and obtain the variation difference.

sentences.zh: 以加減中晷常數，冬至後，中前以差減，中後以差加。

translations.literal: Add or subtract to the mean noon gnomon constant: after Winter Solstice, before noon subtract the difference, after noon add it.
translations.idiomatic: Apply it to the mean noon gnomon constant: after Winter Solstice, subtract before noon and add after noon.

sentences.zh: 夏至後，中前以差加，中後以差減。

translations.literal: After Summer Solstice, before noon add the difference, after noon subtract it.
translations.idiomatic: After Summer Solstice, add before noon and subtract after noon.

translations.literal: On Winter Solstice day, there is decrease but no increase.
translations.idiomatic: On Winter Solstice day, only decrease applies—no increase.

translations.literal: On Summer Solstice day, there is increase but no decrease.
translations.idiomatic: On Summer Solstice day, only increase applies—no decrease.

translations.literal: Obtain the daily fixed noon gnomon count.
translations.idiomatic: This yields the daily fixed noon gnomon count.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，滿象積為刻，不滿為分。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; when full of image accumulation, it becomes clepsydra marks; what does not fill becomes parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane again; carry image accumulation into clepsydra marks, leaving the remainder as parts.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息減、消加其氣初夜半漏，得每日夜半漏定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial midnight clepsydra leak, obtaining the daily fixed midnight leak count.
translations.idiomatic: Successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening midnight leak to obtain the daily fixed midnight leak.

sentences.zh: 其全刻，以九千一百二十乘之，十九乘刻分從之，如三百而一，為晨初餘數。

translations.literal: For the whole marks, multiply by 9,120; let 19 times the mark parts follow; as one per 300, obtaining the dawn-opening remainder count.
translations.idiomatic: For whole marks, multiply by 9,120, add 19 times the fractional marks, divide by 300, and obtain the dawn-opening remainder.

translations.literal: For each, double the midnight leak to obtain night marks.
translations.idiomatic: Double the midnight leak to obtain night clepsydra marks.

translations.literal: Subtract from 100 marks; the remainder is day marks.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from 100 marks; the remainder is day marks.

sentences.zh: 減晝五刻以加夜，即晝為見刻，夜為沒刻。

translations.literal: Subtract five day marks and add to night, then day becomes appearance marks and night becomes disappearance marks.
translations.idiomatic: Move five marks from day to night: day marks become appearance marks, night marks disappearance marks.

sentences.zh: 半沒刻加半辰，起子初算外，得日出辰刻。

translations.literal: Add half the disappearance marks to half a chronogram; starting from outside the zi-opening count, obtain the sunrise chronogram mark.
translations.idiomatic: Add half disappearance marks to half a chronogram; count outward from the zi-opening tally to obtain sunrise chronogram marks.

sentences.zh: 以見刻加而命之，得日入。

translations.literal: Add appearance marks and assign it, obtaining sunset.
translations.idiomatic: Add appearance marks and assign the count to obtain sunset.

sentences.zh: 置夜刻，五而一，得每更差刻。

translations.literal: Set night marks; divide by five to obtain the per-watch difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Set night marks, divide by five, and obtain the per-watch mark difference.

translations.literal: Again divide by five to obtain the per-stave difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by five again for the per-stave mark difference.

sentences.zh: 以昏刻加日入辰刻，得甲夜初刻。

translations.literal: Add dusk marks to the sunset chronogram mark, obtaining the first watch of night A.
translations.idiomatic: Add dusk marks to the sunset chronogram mark to obtain the first watch of night A.

sentences.zh: 又以更籌差加之，得五夜更籌所當辰。

translations.literal: Again add the watch-stave difference to obtain the chronogram for each watch and stave of the five night watches.
translations.idiomatic: Add the watch-stave difference repeatedly to obtain the chronogram for each watch and stave of the five night watches.

sentences.zh: 其夜半定漏，亦名晨初夜刻。

translations.literal: The fixed midnight leak is also called dawn-opening night marks.
translations.idiomatic: The fixed midnight leak is also called dawn-opening night marks.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，滿百為度，不滿為分。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; when full, 100 become degrees; what does not fill becomes parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane again; carry hundreds into degrees, leaving the remainder as parts.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息減、消加氣初去極度，各得每日去極定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial departure from the pole, each obtaining the daily fixed departure from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening polar distance to obtain the daily fixed polar distance.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，以萬二千三百八十六乘之，如萬六千二百七十七而一，為度差。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; multiply by 12,386; as one per 16,277, obtaining the degree difference.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane, multiply by 12,386, divide by 16,277, and obtain the degree difference.

translations.literal: When the difference fills 100, it becomes degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the difference fills 100, carry into degrees.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息加、消減其氣初距中度，得每日距中度定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession add on waning breath and subtract on growing breath from the qi’s initial distance to culminating, obtaining the daily fixed distance to culminating.
translations.idiomatic: Successively add on waning breath and subtract on growing breath from the qi’s opening distance to culmination to obtain the daily fixed culminating distance.

sentences.zh: 倍之，以減周天，為距子度。

translations.literal: Double it; subtract from the circuit of heaven to obtain the distance from zi.
translations.idiomatic: Double it, subtract from the circuit of heaven, and obtain the distance from zi.

sentences.zh: 置其日赤道日度，加距中度，得昏中星。

translations.literal: Set that day’s equatorial solar degree; add the distance to culmination to obtain the dusk culminating star.
translations.idiomatic: Take the day’s equatorial solar longitude, add culminating distance, and obtain the dusk culminating star.

sentences.zh: 倍距子度，以加昏中星，得曉中星。

translations.literal: Double the distance from zi; add to the dusk culminating star to obtain the dawn culminating star.
translations.idiomatic: Double the distance from zi, add to the dusk star, and obtain the dawn culminating star.

sentences.zh: 命昏中星為甲夜中星，加每更差度，得五夜中星。

translations.literal: Assign the dusk culminating star as the night-A culminating star; add the per-watch degree difference to obtain the culminating stars for the five night watches.
translations.idiomatic: Take the dusk culminating star as night A’s culminating star; add the per-watch degree difference for each of the five night watches.

sentences.zh: 凡九服所在，每氣初日中晷常數不齊。

translations.literal: In general, wherever the nine domains lie, the mean noon gnomon constants at each qi’s opening are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Across the nine domains, the mean noon gnomon constants at each qi’s opening are not uniform.

sentences.zh: 使每氣去極度數相減，各為其氣消息定數。

translations.literal: Have each qi’s departure-from-pole numbers subtract from one another; each difference is that qi’s fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract each qi’s polar distances pairwise; each difference is that qi’s fixed message count.

sentences.zh: 因測其地二至日晷，測一至可矣，不必兼要冬夏。

translations.literal: Then measure that place’s solstitial gnomon; measuring one solstice suffices—there is no need to require both winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Measure the locality’s solstitial gnomon; one solstice suffices—both winter and summer need not be taken.

sentences.zh: 於其戴日之北每度晷數中，較取長短同者，以為其地戴日北度數及分。

translations.literal: Among the per-degree gnomon counts north of the sub-solar point, compare and take those of equal length and shortness as that place’s degrees and parts north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Among per-degree gnomon counts north of the sub-solar point, match equal shadow lengths to fix that place’s degrees and parts north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 每氣各以消息定數加減之，因冬至後者，每氣以減。

translations.literal: For each qi, add or subtract by its fixed message count; for those after Winter Solstice, each qi subtracts.
translations.idiomatic: For each qi, apply its fixed message count; after Winter Solstice, subtract for each qi.

translations.literal: For those after Summer Solstice, each qi adds.
translations.idiomatic: After Summer Solstice, add for each qi.

translations.literal: Obtain each qi’s degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: This yields each qi’s degrees north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各因所直度分之晷數，為其地每定氣初日中晷常數。

translations.literal: For each, take the gnomon count for its degree and parts as that place’s fixed mean noon gnomon constant at each qi’s opening.
translations.idiomatic: Take the gnomon count at each degree and part as that locality’s fixed mean noon gnomon constant at each qi’s opening.

sentences.zh: 其測晷有在表南者，亦據其晷尺寸長短與戴日北每度晷數同者，因取其所直之度，去戴日北度數。

translations.literal: If the measured gnomon falls south of the table, likewise according to whether its gnomon’s size, length, and shortness match the per-degree counts north of the sub-solar point, thereby take the degree it corresponds to and subtract from the degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: If the measured shadow falls south of the table, match its length to the north-of-sub-solar per-degree table, take the corresponding degree, and subtract from degrees north of the sub-solar point.

translations.literal: Reverse it to obtain degrees south of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Reverse the sign to obtain degrees south of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 然後以消息定數加減之。

translations.literal: Then add or subtract by the fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Then apply the fixed message count by addition or subtraction.

sentences.zh: 二至各於其地下水漏以定當處晝夜刻數。

translations.literal: At each solstice, fix the day-and-night clepsydra marks for that place’s water clock to determine the local day and night mark count.
translations.idiomatic: At each solstice, calibrate the local water clock to fix the day-and-night clepsydra marks for that place.

translations.literal: Then subtract to obtain the solstitial difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the two to obtain the solstitial mark difference.

sentences.zh: 半之，以加減二至晝夜刻數，為定春秋分初日晝夜刻數。

translations.literal: Halve it; add or subtract to the solstitial day-and-night mark counts to obtain the fixed spring and autumn equinox opening day-and-night mark counts.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the difference and apply it to the solstitial day-night marks to fix the spring and autumn equinox opening day-night marks.

translations.literal: Then set each qi’s fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Then set each qi’s fixed message count.

sentences.zh: 以當處差刻數乘之，如二至去極差度四十七分，八十而一，所得依分前後加減初日晝夜漏刻，各得餘定氣初日晝夜漏刻。

translations.literal: Multiply by the local mark difference; as one per the solstitial departure-from-pole difference of 47 parts 80, obtaining according to parts before and after to add or subtract the opening day-and-night leak marks, each obtaining the remaining fixed qi’s opening day-and-night leak marks.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the local mark difference, divide by the solstitial polar-distance span (47 parts 80), and add or subtract the opening day-night leak marks by fractional rank to obtain each remaining fixed qi’s opening day-night leaks.

sentences.zh: 置每日消息定衰，亦以差刻乘之，差度而一，所得以息減、消加其氣初漏刻，得次日。

translations.literal: Set the daily fixed message wane; likewise multiply by the mark difference; as one per degree difference, obtaining to subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s opening leak marks, obtaining the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Take the daily fixed message wane, multiply by the mark difference, divide by the degree difference, and step the qi’s opening leaks by waning breath and growing breath to obtain the next day.

sentences.zh: 其求距中度及昏明中星日出入，皆依陽城法求之。

translations.literal: In seeking the distance to culmination and the dusk, dawn, and culminating stars and the sun’s entry and exit, all follow the Yangcheng method.
translations.idiomatic: Distance to culmination, dusk and dawn culminating stars, and sunrise and sunset are all found by the Yangcheng method.

sentences.zh: 仍以差刻乘之，差度而一，為今有之數。

translations.literal: Still multiply by the mark difference; as one per degree difference, this is the present-part count.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the mark difference and divide by the degree difference for the present-part correction.

sentences.zh: 若置其地春秋定日中晷常數與陽城每日晷數，較其同者，因其日夜半漏亦為其地定春秋分初日夜半漏。

translations.literal: If one sets that place’s fixed spring and autumn equinox mean noon gnomon constant against Yangcheng’s daily gnomon counts and compares for agreement, then according to its day the midnight leak also becomes that place’s fixed spring and autumn equinox opening midnight leak.
translations.idiomatic: Match the locality’s fixed equinox mean noon gnomon to Yangcheng’s daily table; on the matching day, its midnight leak becomes the locality’s fixed equinox opening midnight leak.

sentences.zh: 求餘定氣初日，亦以消息定數依分前後加減刻分，春分後以減，秋分後以加。

translations.literal: To seek the remaining fixed qi’s opening day, likewise use the fixed message count to add or subtract marks and parts before and after the fractional rank; after the spring equinox subtract, after the autumn equinox add.
translations.idiomatic: For each remaining fixed qi’s opening day, apply the fixed message count to marks and parts by fractional rank—subtract after spring equinox, add after autumn equinox.

translations.literal: When full of image accumulation, it becomes marks.
translations.idiomatic: Carry image accumulation into clepsydra marks.

sentences.zh: 求次日，亦以消息定衰，依陽城術求之。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, likewise use the fixed message wane and follow the Yangcheng procedure.
translations.idiomatic: For the next day, step the fixed message wane by the Yangcheng procedure.

translations.literal: This method exhausts the principle and in the main accords with thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: This method plumbs the principle and is broadly sound.

translations.literal: Yet on high mountains and level plains, viewing the sun is not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mountain heights and level plains do not present the sun equally.

translations.literal: Compare their day gnomons; only then are length and shortness the same.
translations.idiomatic: Only when their noon shadows are compared do lengths agree.

translations.literal: Examine their water leaks; many and few differ markedly.
translations.idiomatic: Water-clock flows differ greatly in rate.

translations.literal: By this cross-check, the prior method is the sounder.
translations.idiomatic: On this comparison, the earlier method is the more reliable.

sentences.zh: 終數八億二千七百二十五萬一千三百二十二。
交終日二十七，餘六百四十五，秒千三百二十二。
中日十三，餘千八百四十二，秒五千六百六十一。
朔差日二，餘九百六十七，秒八千六百七十八。
望差日一，餘四百八十三，秒九千三百三十九。
望數日十四，餘二千三百二十六，秒五千。
交限日十二，餘千三百五十八，秒六千三百二十二。

translations.literal: Remove the conjunction number from the new-moon accumulated parts;
translations.idiomatic: Divide the new-moon accumulated parts by the conjunction number;

sentences.zh: 不盡，以秒法乘之，盈交數又去之；

translations.literal: what does not exhaust, multiply by the seconds divisor; what fills the conjunction number, remove again;
translations.idiomatic: take the remainder, multiply by the seconds divisor, divide again by the conjunction number;

sentences.zh: 餘如秒法而一，為入交分。

translations.literal: the remainder as one per seconds divisor becomes the entry-conjunction parts.
translations.idiomatic: divide the remainder by the seconds divisor to obtain entry-conjunction parts.

sentences.zh: 滿通法為日，命日算外，得天正經朔加時入交汎日及餘。

translations.literal: When full of the universal divisor, it becomes days; assign outside the day count, obtaining the heavenly standard canonical new moon’s added-time entry-conjunction general day and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Carry the universal divisor into days; count outward from the day tally to obtain the standard new moon’s added-time general conjunction day and remainder.

translations.literal: Thereby add the new-moon difference to obtain the next new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add the new-moon interval to obtain the next new moon.

translations.literal: Add the full-moon count to the new moon to obtain the full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add the full-moon count to the new moon to obtain full moon.

sentences.zh: 若以經朔望小餘減之，各得夜半所入。

translations.literal: If one subtracts the canonical new- and full-moon minor remainders, each obtains midnight entry.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the canonical new- and full-moon minor remainders to obtain midnight entry for each.

translations.literal: Accumulate by adding one day to obtain the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Add one day cumulatively to obtain the next day.

translations.literal: When the addition fills the conjunction termination, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: When the sum fills the synodic month, discard the cycle.

sentences.zh: 各以其日入氣朓朒定數，朓減、朒加交汎，為入交常日及餘。

translations.literal: For each, take that day’s entry qi tiao-tuo fixed count; tiao subtracts and tuo adds to the general conjunction, becoming the entry-conjunction regular day and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Apply that day’s qi tiao-tuo correction—tiao subtracts, tuo adds—to the general conjunction for the regular conjunction day and remainder.

sentences.zh: 又以交率乘其日入轉朓朒定數，如交數而一，以朓減、朒加入交常，為入交定日及餘。

translations.literal: Again multiply that day’s entry rotation tiao-tuo fixed count by the conjunction rate; as one per conjunction number, tiao subtracts and tuo adds to the regular conjunction, becoming the entry-conjunction fixed day and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the day’s rotation tiao-tuo correction by the conjunction rate, divide by the conjunction number, and apply tiao/tuo to the regular conjunction for the fixed conjunction day and remainder.

sentences.zh: 各如中日已下者，為月入陽曆；

translations.literal: Each like median day and below is the moon entering the yang calendar;
translations.idiomatic: If not above the half-month interval, the moon is in the yang half of the cycle;

sentences.zh: 已上者，去之，餘為月入陰曆。

translations.literal: if above, remove it; the remainder is the moon entering the yin calendar.
translations.idiomatic: if above, discard the half-month; the remainder is entry into the yin half.

translations.literal: Moon’s departure from the Yellow Path in degrees

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰初　加百八十七

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, line 1: add 187

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰二　加百七十一

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, line 2: add 171

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰三　加百四十七

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, line 3: add 147

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰四　加百一十五

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, line 4: add 115

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰五　加七十五

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, line 5: add 75

sentences.zh: 少陽少陰上　加二十七

translations.literal: Lesser Yang, Lesser Yin, top line: add 27
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Yang / Lesser Yin, top line: +27

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰初　減二十七

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, line 1: subtract 27

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰二　減七十五

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, line 2: subtract 75

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰三　減百一十五

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, line 3: subtract 115

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰四　減百四十七

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, line 4: subtract 147

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰五　減百七十一

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, line 5: subtract 171

sentences.zh: 老陽老陰上　減百八十七

translations.literal: Greater Yang, Greater Yin, top line: subtract 187
translations.idiomatic: Greater Yang / Greater Yin, top line: −187

sentences.zh: 以其爻加減率與後爻加減率相減，為前差。

translations.literal: Subtract that line’s increment-decrement rate from the next line’s increment-decrement rate, obtaining the forward difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract this line’s rate from the next line’s rate to obtain the forward difference.

sentences.zh: 又以後爻率與次後爻率相減，為後差。

translations.literal: Again subtract the next line’s rate from the line after that’s rate, obtaining the rear difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the next line’s rate from the following line’s rate to obtain the rear difference.

translations.literal: Subtract the two differences to obtain the middle difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the two differences to obtain the middle difference.

sentences.zh: 置所在爻幷後爻加減率，半中差以加而半之，十五而一，為爻末率，因為後爻初率。

translations.literal: Set the line’s place together with the next line’s increment-decrement rate; add half the middle difference and halve it; as one per fifteen, obtaining the line’s terminal rate, thereby becoming the next line’s opening rate.
translations.idiomatic: Take the line and next line’s rates, add half the middle difference and halve, divide by 15 for the line’s terminal rate—which becomes the next line’s opening rate.

sentences.zh: 每以本爻初、末率相減，為爻差。

translations.literal: Each time subtract this line’s opening and terminal rates to obtain the line difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract opening from terminal rate each line to obtain the line difference.

translations.literal: As one per fifteen, obtaining the degree difference.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 15 to obtain the per-degree difference.

sentences.zh: 半之，以加減初率，少象減之，老象加之。

translations.literal: Halve it; add or subtract to the opening rate—lesser images subtract it, greater images add it—becoming the fixed opening rate.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the degree difference; apply to the opening rate—subtract for lesser images, add for greater—to fix the opening rate.
This is the fixed opening rate.

sentences.zh: 每以度差累加減之，少象以差減，老象以差加。

translations.literal: Each time accumulate add or subtract by the degree difference—lesser images subtract the difference, greater images add it—each obtaining the fixed increment-decrement parts for each degree.
translations.idiomatic: Step by the degree difference—subtract for lesser images, add for greater—to obtain fixed per-degree increment-decrement parts.

translations.literal: Each obtaining the fixed increment-decrement parts for each degree.
translations.idiomatic: Each step yields fixed per-degree parts.

sentences.zh: 迺循積其分，滿百二十為度，各為月去黃道數及分。

translations.literal: Then circulate and accumulate the parts; when full, 120 become degrees, each becoming the moon’s departure from the Yellow Path in degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the parts cumulatively; at 120 carry into degrees to obtain lunar latitude in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 其四象初爻無初率，上爻無末率，皆倍本爻加減率，十五而一。

translations.literal: The four images’ opening lines have no opening rate; the top lines have no terminal rate—each doubles that image’s increment-decrement rate and takes one per fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Opening lines of the four images lack an opening rate; top lines lack a terminal rate—double the image’s rate and divide by 15.

sentences.zh: 所得，各以初、末率減之，皆互得其率。

translations.literal: What is obtained, each subtracts from the opening and terminal rates; each mutually obtains its rate.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the result from opening and terminal rates to recover the paired rates.

sentences.zh: 各置夜半入轉，以夜半入交定日及餘減之，不足減，加轉終。

translations.literal: For each, set midnight entry rotation; subtract midnight entry-conjunction fixed day and remainder; if insufficient, add the rotation termination.
translations.idiomatic: Set midnight rotation entry, subtract fixed conjunction day and remainder, adding the rotation cycle if needed.

sentences.zh: 餘為定交初日夜半入轉。

translations.literal: The remainder is the fixed conjunction opening midnight entry rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder is fixed-conjunction opening midnight rotation entry.

sentences.zh: 乃以定交初日與其日夜半入餘，各乘其日轉定分，如通法而一，為分。

translations.literal: Then take the fixed conjunction opening day and its midnight entry remainder; each multiply by that day’s rotation fixed parts; as one per universal divisor, obtaining parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fixed conjunction opening day and midnight remainder each by that day’s rotation fixed parts; divide by the universal divisor for parts.

translations.literal: When full of the rotation divisor, it becomes degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Carry the rotation divisor into degrees.

sentences.zh: 各以加其日轉積度分，乃相減，所餘為其日夜半月行入陰陽度數。

translations.literal: Each add to that day’s rotation accumulated degrees and parts; then subtract, and the remainder is that day and night’s half-month motion’s entry into yin-yang degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Add to the day’s rotation accumulation, then subtract; the remainder is half-month motion into yin-yang degrees and parts for that day and night.

sentences.zh: 轉求次日，以轉定分加之。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add the rotation fixed parts.
translations.idiomatic: For the next day, add the rotation fixed parts.

sentences.zh: 以一象之度九十除之，若以少象除之，則兼除差度一、度分百六、大分十三、小分十四。

translations.literal: Divide by one image’s 90 degrees; if dividing by a lesser image, then also divide the difference degree 1, degree parts 106, major parts 13, and minor parts 14.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 90° per image; for a lesser image, also remove difference 1°, 106 parts, 13 major, 14 minor.

translations.literal: When finished, then divide by the next image in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Then divide by successive images in order.

sentences.zh: 所得以少陽、老陽、少陰、老陰為次，起少陽算外，得所入象度數及分。

translations.literal: What is obtained, take Lesser Yang, Greater Yang, Lesser Yin, Greater Yin in sequence, starting from outside the Lesser Yang count, obtaining the entered image’s degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Take the quotient in Lesser Yang, Greater Yang, Lesser Yin, Greater Yin order, counting from outside Lesser Yang, for image degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 先以三十乘陰陽度分，十九而一，為度分。

translations.literal: First multiply the yin-yang degree parts by 30; as one per nineteen, obtaining degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply yin-yang fractional parts by 30 and divide by 19 for degree parts.

sentences.zh: 不盡，以十五乘、十九除，為大分。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust, multiply by 15 and divide by 19, obtaining major parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the remainder by 15, divide by 19, for major parts.

sentences.zh: 不盡者，又乘，又除，為小分。

translations.literal: What still does not exhaust, again multiply and again divide, obtaining minor parts.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat multiply-and-divide for minor parts on the remainder.

translations.literal: Then divide by the image’s degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Then divide by the image degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 乃以一爻之度十五除之，得所入爻度數及分。

translations.literal: Then divide by one line’s 15 degrees to obtain the entered line’s degrees and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by 15° per line to obtain line degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 其月行入少象初爻之內及老象上爻之中，皆沾黃道。

translations.literal: When the moon’s motion enters within the opening line of a lesser image or within the top line of a greater image, it touches the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon enters inside a lesser image’s opening line or a greater image’s top line, it meets the ecliptic.

translations.literal: At new or full moon, there may be wane and eclipse.

sentences.zh: 凡入交定如望差已下，交限已上，為入蝕限。

translations.literal: In general, fixed entry like full-moon difference and below, conjunction limit and above, is entry into the eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed entry from full-moon difference up to conjunction limit defines the eclipse window.

translations.literal: Full moon entering the eclipse limit, then lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Full moon within the eclipse limit yields lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 朔入蝕限，月在陰曆，則日蝕。

translations.literal: New moon entering the eclipse limit, with the moon in the yin calendar, then solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: New moon within the limit while the moon is in the yin half yields solar eclipse.

translations.literal: Like full-moon difference and below is after conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: At or below the full-moon difference is after conjunction.

sentences.zh: 交限已上，以減交中，餘為交前。

translations.literal: Conjunction limit and above—subtract from conjunction median—the remainder is before conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: At or above the conjunction limit, subtract from the half-month interval; the remainder is before conjunction.

sentences.zh: 置交前後定日及餘，通之，為去交前後定分。

translations.literal: Set the fixed days and remainders before and after conjunction; reduce them to common parts to obtain the fixed parts before and after conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Set before- and after-conjunction fixed days and remainders and reduce to common parts from conjunction.

sentences.zh: 十一乘之，二千六百四十三除，為去交度數。

translations.literal: Multiply by 11; divide by 2,643 to obtain the degrees from conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 11, divide by 2,643, for degrees from conjunction.

sentences.zh: 不盡，以通法乘之，復除為餘。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust, multiply by the universal divisor and divide again for the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: On remainder, multiply by the universal divisor and divide again.

sentences.zh: 大抵去交十三度已上，雖入蝕限，為涉交數微，光景相接，或不見蝕。

translations.literal: In general, from conjunction 13 degrees and above, though within the eclipse limit, because the crossing number is slight and radiance meets, eclipse may not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, beyond 13° from conjunction, even inside the eclipse limit, shallow crossing and grazing light may hide the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 望去交分七百七十九已下者，皆既。

translations.literal: For departure from conjunction parts 779 and below, all are total.
translations.idiomatic: Departure from conjunction of 779 parts or less is always total.

sentences.zh: 已上者，以定交分減望差，餘以百八十三約之，命以十五為限，得月蝕之大分。

translations.literal: Above that, subtract the fixed conjunction parts from the full-moon difference; the remainder, reduced by 183, assign with 15 as limit, obtaining the lunar eclipse’s major parts.
translations.idiomatic: Above that, subtract fixed conjunction parts from full-moon difference; divide the remainder by 183 with limit 15 for the lunar eclipse magnitude in major parts.

sentences.zh: 月在陰曆，初起東南，甚於正南，復於西南。

translations.literal: With the moon in the yin calendar, it first rises southeast, culminates due south, then sets southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Moon in the yin half: first visible southeast, greatest at south, then southwest.

sentences.zh: 月在陽曆，初起東北，甚於正北，復於西北。

translations.literal: With the moon in the yang calendar, it first rises northeast, culminates due north, then sets northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Moon in the yang half: first visible northeast, greatest at north, then northwest.

sentences.zh: 其蝕十二分已上者，起於正東，復於正西。

translations.literal: For eclipses of twelve parts and above, they rise due east and set due west.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses of twelve parts or greater rise due east and set due west.

translations.literal: This is discussed according to noon proper.
translations.idiomatic: This assumes noon as the reference.

sentences.zh: 餘各隨方面所在，準此取正。

translations.literal: For the rest, each follows its direction’s location; take correctness by this standard.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere adjust for local direction against this standard.

sentences.zh: 凡月蝕之大分五已下，因增三。

translations.literal: In general, for lunar eclipse major parts five and below, thereby add three.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipse magnitude five parts or less, add three.

translations.literal: Ten and below, thereby add four.

sentences.zh: 其去交定分五百二十已下，又增半。

translations.literal: For fixed departure from conjunction parts 520 and below, again add half.
translations.idiomatic: At 520 parts from conjunction or less, add another half increment.
At 260 or less, add half again.

translations.literal: Each becomes the general-use mark rate.
translations.idiomatic: Each yields the general eclipse duration rate.

sentences.zh: 以所入氣幷後氣增損差，倍六爻乘之，綜兩氣辰數除之，為氣末率。

translations.literal: Take the entered qi together with the next qi’s increase-decrease difference; double the six lines and multiply; divide by the two qi’s chronogram count, obtaining the qi’s terminal rate.
translations.idiomatic: Combine the qi and next qi’s increase-decrease difference, double the six lines, multiply, and divide by both qi’s chronogram count for the qi terminal rate.

sentences.zh: 又列二氣增損差，皆倍六爻乘之，各如辰數而一；

translations.literal: Again set the two qi’s increase-decrease differences; each double the six lines and multiply; each as one per chronogram count;
translations.idiomatic: Set both qi’s differences, double six lines each, and divide each by its chronogram count;

translations.literal: subtract the lesser from the greater; the remainder is the qi difference.
translations.idiomatic: subtract the smaller from the larger; the remainder is the qi difference.

sentences.zh: 加減末率，冬至後以差減，夏至後以差加。

translations.literal: Add or subtract to the terminal rate; after Winter Solstice subtract the difference, after Summer Solstice add it.
translations.idiomatic: Apply to the terminal rate: subtract after Winter Solstice, add after Summer Solstice.

sentences.zh: 倍氣差，綜兩氣辰數除，為日差。

translations.literal: Double the qi difference; divide by the two qi’s chronogram count, obtaining the daily difference.
translations.idiomatic: Double the qi difference and divide by both chronogram counts for the daily difference.

translations.literal: Halve it; add or subtract to opening and terminal, becoming the fixed rate.
translations.idiomatic: Halve it and apply to opening and terminal for the fixed rate.

sentences.zh: 以差累加減氣初定率，冬至後以差加，夏至後以差減。

translations.literal: Accumulate add or subtract by the difference to the qi’s opening fixed rate; after Winter Solstice add the difference, after Summer Solstice subtract it.
translations.idiomatic: Step the qi’s opening fixed rate by the difference—add after Winter Solstice, subtract after Summer Solstice.
This yields the daily increase-decrease difference.

sentences.zh: 及循積之，隨所入氣日增損氣下差積，各其日定數。

translations.literal: And circulate and accumulate it; as one enters the qi’s day, increase or decrease the difference accumulation beneath the qi, each its day’s fixed count.
translations.idiomatic: Sum cumulatively; for each day in the qi, adjust the qi’s difference accumulation to obtain that day’s fixed count.

sentences.zh: 其二至之前一氣，皆後無同差，不可相幷，各因前末為初率。

translations.literal: For the single qi before each solstice, afterward there is no matching difference and they cannot be merged; each takes the prior terminal as opening rate.
translations.idiomatic: The lone qi before each solstice lacks a paired difference; each takes the prior terminal rate as its opening rate.

sentences.zh: 以氣差冬至前減、夏至前加，為末率。

translations.literal: Use the qi difference—before Winter Solstice subtract, before Summer Solstice add—for the terminal rate.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the qi difference—subtract before Winter Solstice, add before Summer Solstice—for the terminal rate.

sentences.zh: 陰曆蝕差千二百七十五，蝕限三千五百二十四，或限三千六百五十九。

translations.literal: Yin-calendar eclipse difference 1,275; eclipse limit 3,524, or limit 3,659.
translations.idiomatic: Yin-half eclipse correction: 1,275; eclipse limit: 3,524 (alternate limit 3,659).

sentences.zh: 陽曆蝕限百三十五，或限九百七十四。
以蝕朔所入氣日下差積，陰曆減之，陽曆加之，各為朔定差及定限。

translations.literal: Take the eclipse new moon’s entered qi day’s difference accumulation; yin calendar subtracts it, yang calendar adds it, each becoming the new moon’s fixed difference and fixed limit.
translations.idiomatic: Take the eclipse new moon’s qi-day difference accumulation; subtract in the yin half, add in the yang half, for fixed difference and fixed limit.

sentences.zh: 朔在陰曆，去交定分滿蝕定差已上者，為陰曆蝕。

translations.literal: New moon in yin calendar: if departure from conjunction fixed parts fills the eclipse fixed difference and above, it is a yin-calendar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: New moon in the yin half: if parts from conjunction meet or exceed the fixed eclipse difference, a yin-half eclipse occurs.

sentences.zh: 不滿者，雖在陰曆，皆類同陽曆蝕。

translations.literal: If it does not fill, though in yin calendar, all are classed like yang-calendar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: If not, though in the yin half, treat as a yang-half eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其去交定分滿定限已下者，的蝕。

translations.literal: If departure from conjunction fixed parts fills the fixed limit and below, it is a certain eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If parts from conjunction are within the fixed limit, eclipse is certain.

translations.literal: At or-limit and below, partial eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At or below the alternate limit, partial eclipse.

sentences.zh: 陰曆蝕者，置去交定分，以蝕定差減之，餘百四已下者，皆蝕既。

translations.literal: For yin-calendar eclipse, set departure from conjunction fixed parts; subtract the eclipse fixed difference; if the remainder is 104 and below, all are total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Yin-half eclipse: subtract fixed difference from parts from conjunction; remainder ≤104 is always total.

sentences.zh: 其入或限者，以百五十二約之。

translations.literal: If entering the or-limit, reduce by 152.
translations.idiomatic: Under the alternate limit, divide by 152.

sentences.zh: 以減十五，餘為日蝕之大分。

translations.literal: Subtract from fifteen; the remainder is the solar eclipse’s major parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from 15; the remainder is solar eclipse magnitude in major parts.

sentences.zh: 其同陽曆蝕者，其去交定分少於蝕定差六十已下者，皆蝕既。

translations.literal: For those classed like yang-calendar eclipse, if departure from conjunction fixed parts are less than the eclipse fixed difference by 60 and below, all are total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Yang-class eclipses: if parts from conjunction are ≤60 below the fixed difference, always total.

sentences.zh: 已上者，以陽曆蝕定限加去交分，以九十約之。

translations.literal: Above that, add departure from conjunction parts to the yang-calendar eclipse fixed limit; reduce by 90.
translations.idiomatic: Above that, add parts from conjunction to the yang fixed limit and divide by 90.

sentences.zh: 其陽曆蝕者，置去交定分，亦以九十約之。

translations.literal: For yang-calendar eclipse, set departure from conjunction fixed parts; likewise reduce by 90.
translations.idiomatic: Yang-half eclipse: set parts from conjunction and likewise divide by 90.

sentences.zh: 入或限者，以百四十三約之。

translations.literal: If entering the or-limit, reduce by 143.
translations.idiomatic: Under the alternate limit, divide by 143.

translations.literal: All half and below are half-weak.

sentences.zh: 命之，以十五為限，得日蝕之大分。

translations.literal: Assign it; with fifteen as limit, obtain the solar eclipse’s major parts.
translations.idiomatic: Assign with limit 15 for solar eclipse magnitude in major parts.

sentences.zh: 月在陰曆，初起西北，甚於正北，復於東北。

translations.literal: With the moon in yin calendar, it first rises northwest, culminates due north, then sets northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Moon in yin half: first visible northwest, greatest at north, then northeast.

sentences.zh: 月在陽曆，初起西南，甚於正南，復於東南。

translations.literal: With the moon in yang calendar, it first rises southwest, culminates due south, then sets southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Moon in yang half: first visible southwest, greatest at south, then southeast.

sentences.zh: 其蝕十二分已上，皆起於正西，復於正東。

translations.literal: For eclipses of twelve parts and above, all rise due west and set due east.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipses of twelve parts or greater rise due west and set due east.

sentences.zh: 凡日蝕之大分，皆因增二。

translations.literal: In general, for solar eclipse major parts, each thereby adds two.
translations.idiomatic: For solar eclipse magnitude, add two throughout.

sentences.zh: 其陰曆去交定分多於蝕定差七十已下者，又增；

translations.literal: For yin calendar, if departure from conjunction fixed parts exceed the eclipse fixed difference by 70 and below, again add;
translations.idiomatic: Yin half: if parts from conjunction exceed the fixed difference by ≤70, add again;
≤35 below the difference, add half again.

sentences.zh: 其同陽曆去交定分少於蝕定差二十已下者，又增半；

translations.literal: For those classed like yang calendar, if departure from conjunction fixed parts are less than the eclipse fixed difference by 20 and below, again add half;
translations.idiomatic: Yang-class: if parts from conjunction are ≤20 below the fixed difference, add half again;

translations.literal: 4 and below, again add a little.
translations.idiomatic: ≤4 below, add a small increment again.

translations.literal: Each becomes the general-use mark rate.
translations.idiomatic: Each yields the general eclipse duration rate.

sentences.zh: 置去交定分，以交率乘之，二十乘交數除之；

translations.literal: Set departure from conjunction fixed parts; multiply by the conjunction rate; twenty times the conjunction number divides it;
translations.idiomatic: Set parts from conjunction, multiply by the conjunction rate, and divide by twenty times the conjunction number;

sentences.zh: 其月道與黃道同名者，以加朔望定小餘；

translations.literal: if the moon’s path and Yellow Path share the same name, add to the fixed new- or full-moon minor remainder;
translations.idiomatic: if lunar path and ecliptic share the same direction name, add to the fixed syzygy minor remainder;

sentences.zh: 異名者，以減朔、望定小餘：為蝕定餘。

translations.literal: if different names, subtract from the fixed new- or full-moon minor remainder: becoming the eclipse fixed remainder.
translations.idiomatic: if opposite names, subtract from the fixed syzygy minor remainder for the eclipse fixed remainder.

sentences.zh: 如求發斂加時術入之，得蝕甚辰刻。

translations.literal: Like seeking the issuing-and-gathering added-time method, enter it to obtain the eclipse culmination chronogram mark.
translations.idiomatic: Enter by the issuing-and-gathering added-time method to obtain eclipse culmination chronogram marks.

translations.literal: For each, set the general-use mark rate as auxiliary.
translations.idiomatic: Set the general duration rate as auxiliary for each.

sentences.zh: 以乘其日入轉損益率，如通法而一。

translations.literal: Multiply by that day’s entry rotation increase-decrease rate; as one per universal divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by that day’s rotation increase-decrease rate and divide by the universal divisor.

translations.literal: What is obtained, if it answers tuo, increase or decrease accordingly;
translations.idiomatic: Apply the result: if tuo applies, adjust accordingly;

sentences.zh: 應朓者，損加、益減其副：為定用刻數。

translations.literal: if it answers tiao, add to decrease and subtract to increase on the auxiliary: becoming the fixed-use mark count.
translations.idiomatic: if tiao applies, invert the adjustment on the auxiliary for the fixed duration count.

sentences.zh: 半之，以減蝕甚辰刻，為虧初；

translations.literal: Halve it; subtract from the eclipse culmination chronogram mark, obtaining first contact;
translations.idiomatic: Halve it, subtract from eclipse culmination marks for first contact;

translations.literal: add to the eclipse culmination chronogram mark, obtaining last contact.
translations.idiomatic: add to culmination marks for last contact.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕，置定用刻數，以其日每更差刻除，為更數。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse, set the fixed-use mark count; divide by that day’s per-watch mark difference, obtaining watch count.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipse: set fixed duration, divide by per-watch mark difference for watch count.

sentences.zh: 不盡，以每籌差刻除，為籌數。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust, divide by per-stave mark difference, obtaining stave count.
translations.idiomatic: Remainder: divide by per-stave difference for stave count.

translations.literal: Combine them as the fixed-use watches and staves.
translations.idiomatic: Combine for fixed watches and staves.

sentences.zh: 乃累計日入後至蝕甚辰刻，置之，以昏刻加日入辰刻減之，餘以更籌差刻除之。

translations.literal: Then accumulate from after day entry to eclipse culmination chronogram mark and set it; subtract sunset chronogram mark plus dusk marks;
translations.idiomatic: Sum from after day entry to eclipse culmination, subtract sunset plus dusk marks;

sentences.zh: 所得命以初更籌算外，得蝕甚更籌。

translations.literal: what is obtained, assign outside the first-watch stave count, obtaining the eclipse culmination watch and stave.
translations.idiomatic: divide the remainder by watch-stave difference and assign from first watch for culmination watch and stave.

sentences.zh: 半定用更籌減之，為虧初；

translations.literal: Subtract half the fixed-use watches and staves, obtaining first contact;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract half the fixed watches and staves for first contact;

sentences.zh: 按天竺俱摩羅所傳斷日蝕法，日躔鬱車宮者，的蝕。

translations.literal: According to the eclipse-dating method transmitted by Kumāra of India: if the sun lodges in the Yùchē palace, eclipse is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Per Kumāra of India’s eclipse rule: sun in the Yùchē mansion means certain eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其餘據日所在宮，火星在前三及後五之宮，幷伏在日下，則不蝕。

translations.literal: For the rest, according to the palace where the sun stands, if Mars is in the three palaces before and five after, and hidden beneath the sun, then no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if Mars lies three mansions before through five after the sun’s mansion, or is occulted beneath the sun, no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 若五星皆見，又水在陰曆及三星已上同聚一宿，則亦不蝕。

translations.literal: If all five planets are visible, and Mercury is in yin calendar and three stars or more gather in one lodge, then likewise no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If all five planets are visible, Mercury is in the yin half, and three or more stars share one lodge, likewise no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 凡星與日別宮或別宿則易斷，若同宿則難。

translations.literal: In general, if star and sun are in different palaces or different lodges it is easy to judge; if in the same lodge it is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Stars in a different mansion or lodge from the sun are easy to judge; same lodge is hard.

sentences.zh: 天竺所云十二宮，即中國之十二次。

translations.literal: The twelve palaces spoken of in India are precisely China’s twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: India’s twelve palaces are China’s twelve chronogram stations.

translations.literal: The Yùchē palace is the chronogram of Jiànglóu.
translations.idiomatic: Yùchē mansion is the Jiànglóu station.

translations.literal: Across the nine domains, eclipse differences differ.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse corrections differ across the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 先測其地二至及定春秋中晷長短，與陽城每日中晷常數較取同者，各因其日蝕差為其地二至及定春秋分蝕差。

translations.literal: First measure that place’s solstitial and fixed spring-autumn equinox mean noon gnomon lengths; compare with Yangcheng’s daily mean noon gnomon constants and take agreement; each thereby takes that day’s eclipse difference as that place’s solstitial and fixed equinox eclipse difference.
translations.idiomatic: Measure local solstitial and equinox noon shadows, match Yangcheng’s daily table, and adopt that day’s eclipse difference for local solstice and equinox corrections.

sentences.zh: 以夏至差減春分差，以春分差減冬至，各為率。

translations.literal: Subtract spring equinox difference from summer solstice difference; subtract winter solstice from spring equinox difference; each becomes a rate.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract spring from summer solstice difference and winter from spring difference; each is a rate.

sentences.zh: 幷二率，半之，六而一，為夏率。

translations.literal: Combine the two rates; halve; as one per six, obtaining the summer rate.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the rates, halve, divide by six for the summer rate.

sentences.zh: 二率相減，六而一，為總差。

translations.literal: Subtract the two rates; as one per six, obtaining the total difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the rates and divide by six for the total difference.

translations.literal: Set the total difference; as one per six, obtaining the qi difference.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the total difference by six for the per-qi difference.

sentences.zh: 半氣差，以加夏率，又以總差減之，為冬率。

translations.literal: Half the qi difference, add to the summer rate; again subtract the total difference, obtaining the winter rate.
translations.idiomatic: Add half the qi difference to the summer rate, subtract the total difference for the winter rate.

translations.literal: The winter rate is the Winter Solstice rate.
translations.idiomatic: The winter rate is the Winter Solstice rate.

sentences.zh: 每以氣差加之，各為每氣定率。

translations.literal: Each time add the qi difference, each becoming each qi’s fixed rate.
translations.idiomatic: Add the qi difference stepwise for each qi’s fixed rate.

sentences.zh: 乃循積其率，以減冬至蝕差，各得每氣初日蝕差。

translations.literal: Then circulate and accumulate the rates; subtract from the Winter Solstice eclipse difference, each obtaining each qi’s opening day eclipse difference.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the rates cumulatively and subtract from the Winter Solstice eclipse difference for each qi’s opening eclipse correction.

translations.literal: To seek each day, seek it like the Yangcheng method.
translations.idiomatic: For daily values, follow the Yangcheng procedure.

sentences.zh: 若戴日之南，當計所在地，皆反用之。

translations.literal: If south of the sub-solar point, one should reckon the location and use it in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: South of the sub-solar point, reckon the locality and apply the tables in reverse.

translations.literal: Seven: Method for pacing the five planets
translations.idiomatic: VII. Method for Determining the Five Planets

sentences.zh: 終率百二十一萬二千五百七十九，秒六。
終日三百九十八，餘二千六百五十九，秒六。
象算九十一，餘二百三十八，秒五十七，微分十二。
爻算十五，餘百六十六，秒四十二，微分八十二。

終日七百七十九，餘二千八百四十三，秒八十六。
象算九十一，餘二百三十八，秒四十三，微分八十四。
爻算十五，餘百六十六，秒四十，微分六十二。
終率百一十四萬九千三百九十九，秒九十八。
終日三百七十八，餘二百七十九，秒九十八。
象算九十一，餘二百三十七，秒八十七。
爻算十五，餘百六十六，秒三十一，微分十六。
終率百七十七萬五千三十，秒十二。
終日五百八十三，餘二千七百一十一，秒十二。
中合日二百九十一，餘二千八百七十五，秒六。
象算九十一，餘二百三十八，秒三十四，微分五十四。
爻算十五，餘百六十六，秒三十九，微分九。
終率三十五萬二千二百七十九，秒七十二。
終日百一十五，餘二千六百七十九，秒七十二。
中合日五十七，餘二千八百五十九，秒八十六。
變差百三十六，秒七十八。
象算九十一，餘二百四十四，秒九十八，微分六十。
爻算十五，餘百六十七，秒四十九，微分七十四。
置中積分，以冬至小餘減之，各以其星終率去之，不盡者返以減終率；

translations.literal: Set the median accumulated parts; subtract the Winter Solstice minor remainder; each remove by that star’s termination rate; what does not exhaust, return and subtract from the termination rate;
translations.idiomatic: Set median accumulated parts, subtract Winter Solstice minor remainder, divide by each planet’s cycle constant; on remainder, subtract from the cycle constant;

sentences.zh: 餘滿通法為日，得冬至夜半後平合日算。

translations.literal: remainder full of universal divisor becomes days, obtaining the Winter Solstice midnight-after mean-conjunction day count.
translations.idiomatic: carry the universal divisor into days for the Winter Solstice midnight-after mean conjunction day count.

sentences.zh: 各以其星變差乘積算，滿乾實去之；

translations.literal: Each multiply the accumulated count by that star’s variation difference; remove what fills circuit-of-heaven substance;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated count by each planet’s variation difference and remove circuit-of-heaven fills;

translations.literal: remainder full of universal divisor becomes days.

sentences.zh: 以減平合日算，得入曆算數。

translations.literal: Subtract from the mean-conjunction day count, obtaining the entry-epicycle count.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from mean-conjunction day count for entry-epicycle count.

translations.literal: All quarter the remainder alike to match the chronogram divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Quarter all remainders alike to match the chronogram divisor.

sentences.zh: 乃以一象之算除之，以少陽、老陽、少陰、老陰為次，起少陽算外。

translations.literal: Then divide by one image’s count; take Lesser Yang, Greater Yang, Lesser Yin, Greater Yin in sequence, starting from outside the Lesser Yang count.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by one image’s count; take Lesser Yang, Greater Yang, Lesser Yin, Greater Yin in order from outside Lesser Yang.

translations.literal: Remainder divide by one line’s count;
translations.idiomatic: Divide the remainder by one line’s count;

sentences.zh: 以所入爻與後爻損益率相減，為前差。

translations.literal: Subtract the entered line’s increase-decrease rate from the following line’s, as the prior difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the entered line’s increase-decrease rate from the next line’s to obtain the prior difference.

sentences.zh: 又以後爻與次後爻損益率相減，為後差。

translations.literal: Again subtract the following line’s rate from the next-following line’s, as the posterior difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the next line’s rate from the one after it to obtain the posterior difference.

translations.literal: Subtract the two differences; this is the middle difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the two differences to obtain the middle difference.

sentences.zh: 置所入爻幷後爻損益率，半中差以加之，九之，二百七十四而一，為爻末率，因為後爻初率。

translations.literal: Set the entered line together with the following line’s increase-decrease rate; add half the middle difference; multiply by nine; divide by 274 for the line’s terminal rate, which becomes the following line’s initial rate.
translations.idiomatic: Set the entered line and the next line’s increase-decrease rate, add half the middle difference, multiply by nine, and divide by 274 for the line’s terminal rate—which becomes the next line’s initial rate.

sentences.zh: 皆因前爻末率，以為後爻初率。

translations.literal: In each case take the prior line’s terminal rate as the following line’s initial rate.
translations.idiomatic: In each case use the prior line’s terminal rate as the next line’s initial rate.

translations.literal: Subtract initial from terminal rates; this is the line difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the initial from the terminal rate to obtain the line difference.

sentences.zh: 倍爻差，九之，二百七十四而一，為算差。

translations.literal: Double the line difference, multiply by nine, divide by 274; this is the count difference.
translations.idiomatic: Double the line difference, multiply by nine, and divide by 274 to obtain the count difference.

sentences.zh: 半之，加減初、末，各為定率。

translations.literal: Halve it; add or subtract to initial and terminal; each becomes a fixed rate.
translations.idiomatic: Halve it and add or subtract from the initial and terminal values to obtain each fixed rate.

sentences.zh: 以算差累加減爻初定率，少象以差減，老象以差加。

translations.literal: With the count difference cumulatively add or subtract the line’s initial fixed rate; young images subtract the difference, old images add it.
translations.idiomatic: Cumulatively adjust the line’s initial fixed rate by the count difference: young images subtract the difference, old images add it.

translations.literal: This is the increase-decrease rate for each count.
translations.idiomatic: This yields the increase-decrease rate for each count.

sentences.zh: 循累其率，隨所入爻損益其下進退積，各得其算定數。

translations.literal: Accumulate the rates in sequence; according to the entered line increase or decrease the advance-retreat accumulation below, obtaining each count’s fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulate the rates in sequence and, according to the entered line, adjust the advance-retreat accumulation below to obtain each count’s fixed value.

sentences.zh: 其四象初爻無初率，上爻無末率，皆置本爻損益率四而九之，二百七十四得一，各以初、末率減之，皆互得其率。

translations.literal: The four images’ initial lines have no initial rate and top lines no terminal rate; set each line’s native increase-decrease rate, multiply by four and nine, divide by 274; subtract initial and terminal rates from each other to obtain the rates by interchange.
translations.idiomatic: Initial lines of the four images lack an initial rate and top lines lack a terminal rate; set each line’s native increase-decrease rate, multiply by four and nine and divide by 274, then cross-subtract initial and terminal rates to obtain the paired rates.

sentences.zh: 各置其星平合所入爻之算差，半之，以減其入算損益率。

translations.literal: For each star set the count difference of the line entered at mean conjunction; halve it and subtract from the entered-count increase-decrease rate.
translations.idiomatic: For each star set the count difference for the line entered at mean conjunction, halve it, and subtract from the entered-count increase-decrease rate.

sentences.zh: 損者，以所入餘乘差，辰法除，幷差而半之；

translations.literal: For decrease: multiply the entry remainder by the difference, divide by the chronogram method, combine with the difference and halve;
translations.idiomatic: For decrease: multiply the entry remainder by the difference, divide by the chronogram divisor, add the difference and halve;

translations.idiomatic: Set the advance-retreat fixed number; for Venus, double it.

translations.idiomatic: When the quotient fills the chronogram divisor it becomes days; add for advance and subtract for retreat from the mean-conjunction day-count—first quarter-reduce the mean-conjunction remainder, then adjust.

translations.literal: This is the regular conjunction day-count.
translations.idiomatic: This is the regular conjunction day-count.

translations.idiomatic: Set the regular conjunction’s prior-posterior fixed number, divide by four, subtract for prior and add for posterior to the regular conjunction day-count to obtain the fixed conjunction day-count.

sentences.zh: 又四約盈縮分，以定合餘乘之，滿辰法而一；

translations.literal: What is obtained: expansion adds and contraction subtracts from the fixed remainder; add the day-and-night midnight solar degree; this is the fixed-conjunction hour-added star degree.

sentences.zh: 其至朔小餘，皆先以四約之。

sentences.zh: 若大餘不足減，又以爻數加之，乃減之。

sentences.zh: 餘滿四象之策除，為月數。

translations.idiomatic: Divide the remainder by the four-image count to obtain the month-count.

translations.literal: What does not exhaust is the day-count entering new moon.

sentences.zh: 命月起天正、日起經朔算外，得定合月、日。
